S.TRANSL: The girl was an orphan.
She did not have a helper to catch wild animals or pick vegetables.
She went to the river to fish with a fishnet.
She caught no fish with a fishnet.
She found some driftwood instead.
She threw it away.

S.FORM: m-ara-ʔəna-ʔəna=kani r<um>iuʔu par-ətəa-n-ai=kani ʔinia sua sanapisaapiʔi.
S.PHON: maraʔənaʔənakani rumiuʔu parətəanaikani ʔinia sua sanapisaapiʔi
S.TRANSL: She found the driftwood in her fishnet again.
She inserted it on her belt.
"It's my firewood," she said this and went home.
When she was to take it, it was gone.
"I must have lost it." (She thought).
Later on, she became pregnant.
She gave birth to a baby.
He grew up and was skillful.
When he saw a bird, he took aim at it and it fell down.

S.FORM: ara-tatia=kani, panaʔ-ən=kani sua anuka vutunu vavulu, ni-macai=kani.
S.PHON: aratatiakani panaʔənkani sua anuka vutunu vavuɾu nimaʦaikani
S.FORM: aratatiakani, pana'enkani sua anuka vutunu vavuru, nimacaikani.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]atatiakani panaʔenkani sua anuka vutunu vavu[r|ɾ]u nimaʦaikani
S.TRANSL: When he grew up, he shot at the footprints of a deer and wild pig, and they died.
What is in his bag that holds his game?
"Let's cheat him," his (hunting) companions said.

S.PHON: mukusakani rəməra muʦanuma pakisaaikani sua kukunaŋini
S.TRANSL: When they went to the mountains, his companions said to him "Go and fetch water!"

S.FORM: mu-canumu=kani, ala-i=kani sua ku-kunaŋ-ini sua pau-ini putu-vərəka, c<um>əʔəra sua vuur-ini vaava tutui, sua kani rupac-ini taʔiciki=kani.
S.PHON: muʦanumukani aɾaikani sua kukunaŋini sua pauini putuvərəka ʦuməʔəra sua vuurini vaava tutui sua kani rupatʂini taʔitʂikikani
S.FORM: mucanumukani, araikani sua kukunangini sua pauini putuvereka, c<um>e'era sua vuurini vaava tutui, sua kani rupacini ta'icikikani.
S.PHON: muʦanumukani a[r|ɾ]aikani sua kukunaŋini sua pauini putuve[r|ɾ]eka ʦumeʔe[r|ɾ]a sua vuu[r|ɾ]ini vaava tutui sua kani [r|ɾ]upatʂini taʔitʂikikani
S.TRANSL: When he was fetching water, his companions opened his leather bag and found that his bow was made of pig ribs and his arrows made of a shoulder blade.

S.FORM: pu-aiʔi=kani tanasa, na=cina-ini, "c<in>əʔəra cau pau=maku, cina," misa=kani.
S.PHON: puaiʔikani tanasa natʂinaini tʂinəʔəra ʦau paumaku tʂina misakani
S.FORM: puai'ikani tanasa, nacinaini, "c<in>e'era cau paumaku, cina," misakani.
S.PHON: puaiʔikani tanasa natʂinaini tʂineʔe[r|ɾ]a ʦau paumaku tʂina misakani
S.TRANSL: He went home and told his mother, "My leather bag has been looked at by people."
"Gather firewood and cogon grass," he said (to his mother.).
"What is firewood for?" his mother asked.

S.FORM: "tia=maku panaʔ-ən taniarə. nuu maka-sua-ini ia, m-ara-cucua=kita=ʔai lavai."
S.PHON: tiamaku panaʔən taniarə nuu makasuaini ia maraʦuʦuakitaʔai ɾavai
S.FORM: "tiamaku pana'en taniare. nuu makasuaini ia, maracucuakita'ai ravai."
S.PHON: tiamaku panaʔen tania[r|ɾ]e nuu makasuaini ia ma[r|ɾ]aʦuʦuakitaʔai [r|ɾ]avai
S.TRANSL: "I'll go and shoot the sun. If so, I'll go with a friend."
He made a string.
He tied himself with the string to his own house.
He pulled along with the string.
They arrived at the site of the sun.
They concealed themselves.
The sun was rising.

S.PHON: nuu mupanaʔəku ʔinia ɾavai ia musutavərəkitaʔai
S.TRANSL: "When I shoot the sun, friend, let's dive into the water," (he said).
The sun was rising.
He took off his bear leather coat and dropped it (on the ground).
"Who are you? You're staying at my seat," (the sun) said.
The sun was shot by Naparamaci.
He dived into water.

S.FORM: koo=kani paki-sapatə sua vali-ini, panaʔ-ai=kani sa caraʔə taniarə, ni-macai ʔinia.
S.PHON: kookani pakisapatə sua vaɾiini panaʔaikani sa ʦaraʔə taniarə nimaʦai ʔinia
S.FORM: kookani pakisapate sua variini, pana'aikani sa cara'e taniare, nimacai 'inia.
S.PHON: kookani pakisapate sua va[r|ɾ]iini panaʔaikani sa ʦa[r|ɾ]aʔe tania[r|ɾ]e nimaʦai ʔinia
S.TRANSL: His friend could not make it. He was shot by the blood of the sun, and he died.
He returned home by feeling (along the string).
It became dark for a long time.
People had great difficulty.
There was no fuel or food.
They burned their huts.
They dug up sweet potatoes with the light.

S.FORM: kaisisi-ai=kani sua cau sua taniarə s<um>u-avuŋ.
S.PHON: kaiʂiʂiaikani sua ʦau sua taniarə sumuavuŋ
S.FORM: kaisisiaikani sua cau sua taniare s<um>uavung.
S.PHON: kaiʂiʂiaikani sua ʦau sua tania[r|ɾ]e sumuavuŋ
S.TRANSL: People worshiped the sun and offered it with sacrifices.
The sun came (back again).
The sun appeared only briefly and it returned.
The sun set in a short time.
When the sun set, it was fine.
There were two suns in the past.
Naparamaci shot one, and only one was left.
